b6_reason: X_L = 2*pi*50*(50/pi)e-3 = 5 Ohm (clean). Treating R in series with the parallel L-C combination (C's reactance works out to 1000 Ohm, so it carries negligible current and barely loads the L branch), net impedance reduces to about sqrt(R^2+X_L^2) = sqrt(10^2+5^2) = 5*sqrt(5) Ohm, matching option 3 almost exactly.
b6_working: X_L = wL = 2*pi*50*(50/pi)*1e-3 = 5 Ohm. X_C = 1/(wC) = 1/(2*pi*50*(10/pi)*1e-6) = 1000 Ohm (literal value, very large). A plain series R-L-C gives Z = sqrt(R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2) ~= 995 Ohm, which is not among the options, so the figure's topology is not a simple series string of all three. Assuming L and C are in parallel with each other and that pair is in series with R (a common layout for this style of figure), the LC-parallel impedance is j*X_L*X_C/(X_C-X_L) = j*5000/995 ~= j5.03, giving |Z| = sqrt(10^2+5.03^2) ~= 11.19 Ohm, essentially 5*sqrt(5) = 11.18 Ohm.
b6_note: Stem text has no wiring diagram, only component values, so the exact topology is inferred. A literal full series R-L-C gives ~995 Ohm, impossible against these options, so I assumed L parallel C in series with R (C's reactance is so large it barely draws current), which lands almost exactly on option 3. If the real figure wires R, L, C differently, this pick could be wrong -- flagging for the topology to be confirmed against the image.
